Management uses such non-GAAP financial measures to help evaluate our business on a consistent basis, measure our performance, identify trends affecting our business, and assess our operational efficiencies. For the periods presented, Non-core adjustments include: (i) Fintech loan credit enhancement; (ii) Provision for credit losses on fintech loans; (iii) Restructuring costs; (iv) Legal settlement (reimbursement); and (v) Income tax benefits related to a one-time adjustment from purchased transferable tax credits that relate to prior tax years. Non-GAAP measures include: • Adjusted net income is calculated as: GAAP Net income, plus: (i) pre-tax Non-core adjustments, as defined above; (ii) Income tax expense or benefit related to Non-core adjustments; and (iii) Non-core adjustments to Income tax expense. • Core earnings per share is calculated as: Adjusted net income (Non-GAAP), divided by weighted-average diluted shares. • Core revenue is calculated as: the total of GAAP Net interest income and GAAP Non-interest income, less Fintech loan credit enhancement income. • Core non-interest income is calculated as: GAAP Non-interest-income less Fintech loan credit enhancement income. • Core non-interest expense is calculated as: GAAP Non-interest expense, less Non-core adjustments from Restructuring costs and Legal settlement (reimbursement). • Core income tax expense is calculated as: GAAP Income tax expense, less (i) Income tax expense or benefit related to Pre-tax Non-core adjustments; and (ii) Non-core adjustments to Income tax expense related to transferable tax credit carryback. • Core return on assets is calculated as: Adjusted net income (Non-GAAP), divided by Average assets, as reported. • Core return on equity is calculated as: Adjusted net income (Non-GAAP), divided by Average equity, as reported. • Core efficiency ratio is calculated as Core non-interest expense (Non-GAAP) divided by Core revenue (Non-GAAP). This ratio compares revenues generated with the amount of expense required to generate such revenues and may be used as one measure of overall efficiency. • Core non-interest income as a percentage of total revenue is calculated as: (i) Core Non-interest-income (Non-GAAP); divided by (ii) Core revenue (Non-GAAP).
